answer: A trust trellis stops clones at the gate: every new identity needs endorsements from two established agents whose own deposits are slashed if the newcomer misbehaves, so one bad clone sends a ripple of losses through its sponsors. Sponsors therefore only vouch for agents they have actually worked with, and each fake identity costs the attacker fresh, independent sponsors. Reaching the summit earning tier needs several such vouches from unrelated sponsors, so a thousand-clone farm costs a thousand separate bribes instead of one script.
